regulatory_history.title: FTC privacy order against Facebook
regulatory_history.notes: Settled charges that Facebook told users they could keep information private, then let it be shared and made public.

sources.title: US Federal Trade Commission press release
sources.quote: deceived consumers by telling them they could keep their information on Facebook private

regulatory_history.title: $5 billion FTC penalty and a new 20-year privacy order
regulatory_history.notes: Settled charges that Facebook violated its 2012 order by deceiving users about their privacy controls, including sharing friends' data with third-party apps. The court entered the order on 2020-04-23.

sources.title: US Federal Trade Commission press release
sources.quote: $5 billion penalty … deceiving users about their ability to control the privacy

sources.title: US Federal Trade Commission press release
sources.quote: Judge Timothy J. Kelly entered the order on April 23, 2020.

regulatory_history.title: Illinois biometric privacy class action settlement
regulatory_history.notes: Over face templates made for photo tagging without consent, under the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act.

sources.title: AppleInsider
sources.quote: A judge has approved a settlement valued at $650 million from Facebook

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fine over Facebook data scraping
regulatory_history.notes: Decision against Meta Platforms Ireland Limited adopted 2022-11-25: GDPR Articles 25(1) and 25(2), over Facebook Search and the contact importer tools (May 2018 to September 2019).

sources.title: Data Protection Commission (Ireland) press release
sources.quote: imposing a fine of €265 million … collated dataset of Facebook personal data

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fines over the legal basis for Facebook and Instagram processing
regulatory_history.amount: €390 million (€210 million for Facebook, €180 million for Instagram)
regulatory_history.notes: Concerned Meta Ireland's reliance on contract rather than consent, including for behavioural advertising.

sources.title: Data Protection Commission (Ireland) press release
sources.quote: Meta Ireland €210 million (for breaches of the GDPR relating to its Facebook service)

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fine over EU-US transfers of Facebook users' data
regulatory_history.notes: Decision adopted 2023-05-12 under GDPR Article 46(1), following the EDPB's binding decision.

procedural_note.text: Meta said on 2023-05-22 that it would appeal the decision, including the fine.

sources.title: Meta Newsroom
sources.quote: We intend to appeal both the decision's substance and its orders including the fine

sources.title: Data Protection Commission (Ireland) press release
sources.quote: its Facebook service … administrative fine in the amount of €1.2 billion

regulatory_history.title: Texas biometric privacy settlement (Capture or Use of Biometric Identifier Act)
regulatory_history.notes: Texas sued in February 2022 over facial recognition on photos uploaded to Facebook (Tag Suggestions).

sources.title: Texas Attorney General news release
sources.quote: $1.4 billion settlement with Meta … personal biometric data of millions of Texans

sources.title: The Texas Tribune
sources.quote: does not act as an admission of guilt and Meta maintains no wrongdoing

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fine over passwords stored in plaintext
regulatory_history.notes: Meta notified the DPC in 2019 that it had stored some users' passwords without encryption. The release does not name the service.

sources.title: Data Protection Commission (Ireland) press release
sources.quote: stored certain passwords of social media users in 'plaintext' … fine of €91million

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fines over the 2018 Facebook token breach
regulatory_history.notes: About 29 million accounts worldwide, about 3 million in the EU/EEA. Fines: €8 million (Art. 33(3)), €3 million (Art. 33(5)), €130 million (Art. 25(1)), €110 million (Art. 25(2)).

sources.title: Data Protection Commission (Ireland) press release
sources.quote: approximately 29 million Facebook accounts globally … administrative fines totalling €251 million
